NoteClassifier.notes: Written from src/NoteClassifier.cpp at commit b90cd69. The outputs are declared from B down to C but the lookup table note_outputs at line 105 maps note 0 to the C jack and note 11 to the B jack, so the tags follow that table rather than the enum order; the panel draws them as a piano keyboard running from C at the bottom to B at the top. A fault worth knowing: when the enable jack carries exactly one channel reading below 1V, the code skips readVoltages for that port (line 77) but still tests gate[i] for every channel of the pitch input, so channels past the first are compared against uninitialised stack memory. A monophonic gate is therefore only dependable with a monophonic pitch input; give the gate as many channels as the pitch.

RGBMatrix16.notes: src/RGBMatrix.cpp at commit b90cd69; all three sizes are the same template, this one instantiated at 16 by 16. The maker's one-line description in plugin.json calls these an array of lights with built-in oscillators; there are no oscillators in the code. What the X and Y outputs carry is the position of the scan, and its rate comes from the samples-per-pixel knob and the patch's sample rate, so the frame rate is the sample rate divided by the sample count times 256 pixels. The grid of lamps is one widget holding 768 light widgets and no parameters, so no pixel can be clicked for help. In polyphonic mode sixteen pixels are painted per step and the X and Y outputs carry sixteen channels; the grid width must be a multiple of sixteen, which all three sizes are. Double-buffered is on by default and polyphonic mode and fade lights are off.
